items.html:
Confirmed baseline failure: reference-01901–01904 return exactly zero native Mie blocks for a homogeneous sphere with x=80, ε=−8+0.4i, μ=1, κ=0, vacuum host, at l=1,3,80,99. Independent 80/120-digit references are stable; upstream agrees within 1.5e-16–2.9e-14 absolute error. Native maximum absolute errors are approximately 0.500, 0.500, 0.576, 1.60e-8.

Likely cause, source-based inference: unscaled transfer matrices followed by an unsafe-at-extreme-scale 2×2 inverse:

  • coeffs.rs:104 evaluates internal spherical functions without exponential scaling; line 171 accumulates unnormalized transfer amplitudes.
  • line 174 calls nalgebra’s 2×2 inverse. Locked nalgebra 0.35.0 computes cofactors divided by the determinant (inverse.rs:71–80).
  • Locked num-complex 0.4.6 complex division squares the denominator magnitude (lib.rs:819–823). Large, finite determinants can therefore overflow the squared magnitude and yield zero inverse entries.
  • line 176 checks only finiteness, so zero blocks escape detection. The existing robust scalar ratio helper is not used by nalgebra inversion.

The precise intermediate overflow has not been instrumented; this mechanism is strongly consistent with the recorded zeros. Adjoint contamination is plausible because pullback line 201 uses the retained inverse, but gradients in this regime remain unverified.

Collector is calling the correct API. qualify_references.py:394 passes identical parameters directly to each public coeffs.mie; Python forwards them unchanged to _native.mie, which calls mie_forward. No basis conversion occurs. The independent reference explicitly constructs the same helicity block; its metallic convention smoke case already passes at x=1.3.

Coverage gap: this input satisfies the current validation contract. Existing Rust/Hypothesis Mie invariants concentrate on x≤3 and positive dielectric permittivity; upstream oracle tests use sizes≤4 and modest loss. The new qualification is the first inspected coverage of this large metallic regime. Scalar division tests exercise the custom helper, not the matrix inverse. Moreover, an all-zero result can satisfy optical-theorem/passivity equalities, so those invariants alone cannot detect it.

Read-only audit only; no numerical runs, edits, builds, commits, or pushes. Mac/Linux coefficient and binding source hashes match.
